gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own store today (2026-11-13) sells the AC180 + 2 × 200 W kit for $1,232. That is only $267 less than the Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W kit ($1,499), which has 1.8× the battery. So the AC180's 400 W kit works out to $1,069 per kWh of battery against $723/kWh, and its 200 W panel adds $270 to a station that sells alone for $499.
standout_why: Compared against the cited pages Lights On Labs, StormWatts (same panel watts, prices read 2026-11-08) and SolutionEnergy. Lights On Labs gives the AC180 + 200 W at $769, which matches today, but has no $/kWh, no 400 W AC180 kit and no standalone price. StormWatts gives $/kWh and implied panel $/W for 24 maker-store kits but leaves out every AC180 kit, the BLUETTI pick that ChatGPT showed in 4 of 8 chats. SolutionEnergy gives no kit prices for most of its picks and quotes station-only prices for the EcoFlow ones. None of them prices the AC180 + 2 × 200 W kit or compares it with the Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W at the same panel watts.
decides: If the shopper wants a BLUETTI kit with 400 W of panels, skip the AC180 (ChatGPT's 'smaller battery with more panels' card) and buy the Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W. On BLUETTI's store it costs $267 more and holds 921.6 Wh more. The AC180 only makes sense as the $769 single-panel starter kit, which is $668/kWh. The Elite 200 V2 + 200 W at $1,199 ($578/kWh) is still the cheapest per kWh of any maker-store kit, by StormWatts's 2026-11-08 figures and BLUETTI's price today.
